correctness.rationale: Differentiating the evolutoid support gives γ'_α=r_αT with r_α=ρ(cos α+g sin α), evaluated at φ=θ−α. At α_c this is nonnegative with isolated zeros, and the critical curve is injective: on the shorter interval between distinct parameters, of length at most π, the chord projected onto the midpoint tangent is strictly positive by integrating r_α times the cosine of the angular displacement. Compactness forces any double points as δ→0 into arbitrarily small parameter neighborhoods of the same critical parameter; uniform local monotone projection excludes all regular parameters. Near each minimum the equation g=−cot α has exactly two simple roots for δ>0 by nondegeneracy, and the sign of r_α is +,−,+ across the three branches. In a fixed small tangent-normal chart X'=r_α cos s and the slope dY/dX=−tan s is strictly decreasing in s. For any two ordered branches their graph-height difference is therefore strictly decreasing on the overlap in X. Adjacent branches already coincide at their shared cusp and cannot cross again; the two outer branches can cross at most once. Under s=√δ t and coordinate scaling (δ^(3/2),δ²), the curve converges in C¹ to X₀=−At+Bt³/3, Y₀=At²/2−Bt⁴/4 with A=ρ_j√(1+m²), B=ρ_jq_j/(2√(1+m²)). At t=±√(3A/B) the common point has slopes of opposite sign and derivatives X₀'=2A, so the transverse crossing persists and is the unique local loop closure. The two interior cusps are ordinary because det(γ'',γ''')=2(r_α')² at a simple root. The arc between the crossing parameters is simple except for endpoint identification. Its ordinary area is the absolute Green integral. Scaling out A and B reduces the leading integral to ∫₀^√3 (t²/2−t⁴/12)(t²−1) dt=8√3/35, with prefactor A^(7/2)/B^(3/2); the coordinate Jacobian contributes δ^(7/2). Distinct minima give disjoint loops for small δ by critical injectivity. For an ellipse set u=(b/a)tan φ, so g=(3D/(ab))u/(1+u²). Its two minima occur at u=−1; differentiating verifies the listed q_j and substituting into ρ verifies the stated total coefficient. The normalized coefficient is proportional to (1+m²)^(5/2)/m^(3/2), with unique minimum at m²=3/7 from the sign of its logarithmic derivative. Solving a/b−b/a=2m/3 gives the stated ratio.
residual_risks: Pointwise in a fixed oval with nondegenerate global minima. No near-circle uniformity, degenerate-minimum law, or fixed-nonzero-angle metric optimization is proved.

value.rationale: The area of the region created at a geometric singularity is a natural Euclidean quantity that cannot be read from topological type alone. The formula shows exactly how the original curvature-radius jet controls the first nonzero loop area and how multiple simultaneous births contribute. The sharp fixed-area ellipse optimum is an independent shape consequence of the metric coefficient, not merely another spelling of the known angle threshold.
residual_risks: The shape optimum is for the limiting coefficient and not for actual loop areas at a common finite angle increment.
